result_text:
I fixed the four default scoping conventions in `ScopingConventions.java`, so the files they target now land in the generated or build-and-deployment scope. The new regression test and the related existing tests all pass.

Changes, all in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:

- **HTML pages:** the path pattern for the pkgdown, Doxygen and meta-generator rules was `(html|html|xhtml)`. It is now `(html|htm|xhtml)`, which covers `.htm` and keeps `.html` and `.xhtml`. The change is applied to all three rules.
- **.NET documentation XML:** the path `.*/[.]xml` became `.*[.]xml`, so `MyAssembly.xml` matches. The `<doc>` content check still limits it to documentation files.
- **JavaScript generated code:** the path `.*/[.]js` became `.*[.]js`, so `app.js` matches. The `// Generated by …` content check is unchanged.
- **Gradle scripts:** the path `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js` became `.*[-]gradle[.]js`, so `build-gradle.js` matches.

I also added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsDefaultsTest.java`. It checks that the affected conventions match the intended files and leave hand-written `.htm`, `.js` and `.xml` files out. It also checks that `.html`, `.xhtml`, a Doxygen page and `build.gradle` still match.

Test results (offline, `codeanalyzer` module):
- `ScopingConventionsDefaultsTest`: 4 run, 0 failures.
- Existing `SourceFileFilterTest`, `SourceCodeFilesTest` and `CodeConfigurationTest`: all pass.

Nothing is committed.
